claims.text: As-received Q235 steel contains trace or minor levels of Mn and Si in its pre-exposure microstructure.
Mn and Si naturally present in Q235 promote formation of a thin, adherent, multicomponent surface oxide.
The Mn/Si-containing oxide acts as a passivating barrier against aggressive species.
Depleting Mn or Si, or altering their surface distribution, makes the oxide scale less protective and accelerates corrosion.
A mild chemical etch can selectively reduce the surface concentration or alter the distribution of Mn and Si in Q235 steel.
Exposure produces an oxide scale enriched in Mn/Si oxides combined with iron oxides.
Minor alloying elements segregate to the Q235 surface during corrosive exposure.
Surface-segregated Mn and Si react during oxidation to form an adherent mixed oxide layer.
The mixed oxide layer reduces active oxidation and dissolution of iron.
Reducing surface Mn/Si causes increased iron oxidation and dissolution.
Samples retaining or enhancing surface Mn/Si enrichment will have lower mass loss and corrosion rates than Mn/Si-depleted samples.
The proposed protective effect will occur under both ambient chloride/humidity exposure and elevated-temperature exposure at 300–400 °C.
The protective effect requires the oxide scale to remain chemically stable and adherent.
Highly acidic or fluoride-containing environments can override protection by promoting alloy dissolution or disrupting the protective scale.
The quantitative contributions and threshold surface concentrations of Mn and Si required for Q235 passivation are not established.
Failure of Mn/Si-depleted samples to show significantly higher corrosion, poorer passivation, and more extensive damage than untreated controls would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention and experimental design define the treated group as Mn/Si-depleted, whereas the predicted outcome refers to treated samples that retain or enhance Mn/Si enrichment. No enrichment treatment or corresponding experimental group is actually specified.
